summary:
BOO — Orbital Crew Health Watch is an intelligent astronaut health monitoring software built for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge ("Create Health Monitoring Software for Astronauts on Space Missions").  
Long-duration missions expose crews to space radiation, isolation, microgravity-induced bone and muscle loss, and up to 20-minute Mars communication delays. BOO solves this by translating complex physiological data into clear, actionable guidance. Powered by datasets and clinical norms from NASA’s Open Science Data Repository (OSDR), the Human Research Program (HRP), and the Where the ISS at? API, the web platform tracks real-time vitals (HR, SpO_2, temperature, blood pressure, sleep, hydration, and eye pressure) against NASA reference ranges.  
Key features include color-coded Smart Alerts with medical protocols, an Interactive Body Map highlighting organ risk zones, Mars Mode for autonomous onboard decision support, multi-crew and ISS cabin telemetry, and gamified daily health missions. While the software prototype is 100% functional using simulated NASA data, our next milestone integrates physical biometric sensors from the upcoming BOO Smart Helmet for automated real-time synchronization
details:
Project Details: BOO — Orbital Crew Health Watch

1. Project & Challenge Overview

* Project Name: BOO — Orbital Crew Health Watch (BOO Health Ecosystem)

* Event: 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge

* Official Challenge: Create Health Monitoring Software for Astronauts on Space Missions

* Challenge Level & Subjects: Intermediate | Human Exploration, Software, Space Exploration

* Team BOO: Rehab Mohamed Safwat (Team Leader), Mohamed Ibrahim Elsayed Ibrahim, Yousef Ahmed Abdullah Negm, Shahd Ezzat Shabana, and Hana Mahmoud Mohamed.

2. The Problem & Spaceflight Hazards

Long-duration space missions expose astronauts to extreme physiological and psychological risks, including space radiation, isolation, confinement, altered gravity fields, and closed spacecraft environments. Extended microgravity leads to critical health issues such as bone density loss, muscle degradation, fluid shifts, and Spaceflight-Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS). Additionally, deep-space missions—such as voyages to Mars—introduce up to a 20-minute one-way communication delay with Earth, preventing real-time guidance from flight surgeons and creating an urgent need for autonomous on-board health monitoring and decision support.

3. The Solution: BOO Health Ecosystem

BOO is an intelligent, comprehensive astronaut health monitoring software platform designed to translate raw biometric streams into clear, actionable medical guidance:

* Live Vitals & NASA Reference Engine: Tracks real-time physiological indicators—including heart rate, blood oxygen (SpO_2), body temperature, systolic/diastolic blood pressure, blood sugar, sleep duration, mood, eye pressure, and daily hydration—evaluating each metric against published NASA clinical reference ranges.

* Interactive Body Map: Displays an interactive anatomical visualization highlighting organ-specific risk zones in microgravity (such as skeletal bone density and ocular pressure) alongside targeted preventive countermeasures.

* Smart Health Alerts & Protocols: Triggers instant color-coded status alerts (Normal, Watch, Warning, Critical) paired with step-by-step medical action protocols and flight-surgeon escalation workflows.

* Mars Mode & 30-Day Analytics: Features a dedicated Mars Mode that switches the platform to autonomous on-board clinical decision support during deep-space communication delays, complemented by 30-day longitudinal health trend analytics.

* Multi-Crew & ISS Telemetry: Provides commanders and flight surgeons with a unified overview of all crew members' health statuses, cabin environment telemetry, and real-time orbital tracking of the International Space Station (ISS).

* Gamified Daily Health Missions & Guide: Encourages adherence to daily health routines (resistance training, hydration goals, and scheduled vitals checks) through an XP and daily streak system, supported by a built-in NASA spaceflight health guide.

4. Data Sources & NASA Open Resources

* NASA Open Science Data Repository (OSDR): Space biology and human physiology datasets detailing the effects of spaceflight on the cardiovascular, musculoskeletal, and neuro-ocular systems.

* NASA Human Research Program (HRP): Reference frameworks covering the 5 Hazards of Human Spaceflight (space radiation, isolation and confinement, distance from Earth, gravity fields, and hostile/closed environments), Risks of Human Spaceflight, and clinical safety thresholds.

* Where the ISS at? API: Live telemetry feed supplying real-time orbital coordinates, altitude (408\text{ km}), and velocity of the International Space Station.

5. Current Progress & Future Roadmap

* Current Prototype Status (Software — 100% Functional): A complete web-based health monitoring ecosystem featuring live dashboards, simulated NASA biometric datasets across multiple crew profiles, an interactive body map, a clinical alert engine, Mars Mode, and live ISS orbital tracking.

* Future Roadmap (Hardware Integration): Integrating the BOO software platform directly with the upcoming BOO Smart Helmet (BOO Helmet S2) physical biometric sensors to enable automated, continuous helmet-to-dashboard telemetry synchronization without manual logging.
